title: I Took the Habitat Build-Site Hardhat Log to the Foreman Who Waved It

parts.text: I signed the hardhat log at 8:11 a.m. and the foreman waved a cousin onto the roof with no hat. The site rule the foreman posted said: HAT ON BEFORE LADDER. GUESTS IN THE LOG. I was forty-seven, weekend volunteer, holding a loaner that still smelled like soap. Foreman Cal said, "Family knows lumber." I pointed at the rule. He tossed a hammer up. "Lumber doesn't log." I photographed the bare head on the roof, the rule, and the empty log line. Then I took the stills to the site safety lead. At 8:16 safety asked why Cal's name was on a hatless-guest ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Safety can see a bare head on the roof against the hat-before-ladder rule Cal posted.

social.video_title: The foreman waved a cousin up without a hardhat — Part 1/2
social.description: Loaner hat, a roof guest, and a log with an empty line. I walked it to safety. Would you have climbed anyway?

parts.text: Cal called it a minute until safety stopped the roof. I printed the ticket, the rule, and the photo. The cousin logged and hatted. Cal told the porch the rule was always about optics. Optics is a word foremen use when a roof is in a still. Site policy now has a second line: FAMILY KNOWS THE LOG. I hammer. Cal checks heads. The ladder finally has a brim above it.

social.video_title: Family knows the hardhat log — Part 2/2
social.description: Hatless-guest ticket, a stopped roof, and a second line on the rule. Was lumber ever a wave?
